frequency_question: How often are multi-decade transboundary water treaties successfully renewed or extended by the original signatory governments prior to or at expiration?
membership_rule: Includes any formal bilateral or multilateral transboundary water allocation treaty featuring a fixed multi-decade lifespan that reached a critical renewal juncture. Excludes internal water compacts and treaties that dissolved entirely due to state dissolution.

cases.name: US-Canada Columbia River Treaty (provisions extension talks / operational continuity)
India-Pakistan Indus Waters Treaty (ongoing continuous operation past initial milestones without abrogation)
Hungary-Slovakia Gabčíkovo-Nagymaros dispute resolution via interim/extended management frameworks
Israel-Jordan Peace Treaty water annex allocations (routine implementation and renewal)
Senegal River Basin Development Organization (OMVS) convention renewals

coverage_note: 5 named major benchmark cases; total global population of comparable 30-year bilateral water treaties reaching expiry is small, nearly all resulting in renewal or functional rollover due to high sunk costs and mutual dependence.
known_gaps: Limited sample of exactly identical 30-year duration bilateral treaties in densely populated regions with active joint commission frameworks.
skeleton: Global transboundary water treaty renewal events over the last 70 years
multiplier: 5 observed major treaty continuity/renewal milestones out of 5 comparable major historical frameworks reaching maturity
validity_reason: Bilateral water treaty compliance norms and hydropolitical stability baselines change slowly over multi-year periods.
